name: kinetograph
description: Write, check and render Remotion-style TypeScript videos without a browser
readme:
kinetograph.

A blazingly fast programmatic video engine, made for agents.

Kinetograph makes videos from code, without a browser. You (or an agent) write a video in TypeScript with Remotion's API, or as a plain HTML page. Node runs the code, and a Rust GPU compositor draws every frame: CSS, SVG, Canvas 2D, WebGL shaders, 3D and Web Audio. Existing Remotion projects render as they are, and so do [HyperFrames](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes) projects. The film above is one TypeScript project in [`examples/launch`](examples/launch). Kinetograph is in beta (version 0.3.0). APIs can still change between versions. ## Install You need Node.js 22 or newer. The prebuilt package covers macOS on Apple Silicon, Linux x64 and Windows x64, and installs in about a minute with nothing else to set up: ```sh npm install kinetograph npx kinetograph doctor npx kinetograph skills update # agent skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, user-wide ``` Building from source is only for working on the engine, or for a platform with no prebuilt package. It needs Rust and the FFmpeg libraries and takes 15 to 30 minutes: see [Installation: From source](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/getting-started/installation/#from-source). ### Install with a coding agent Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or another coding agent: ```text Set up Kinetograph (https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/kinetograph) for me by following its AGENTS.md: https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/kinetograph/blob/main/AGENTS.md Ask me first whether I want the prebuilt package (recommended) or a build from source, and ask before installing anything system-wide or installing the Kinetograph agent skills. ``` ## Make a video Start a project in an empty folder: ```sh npx kinetograph init # TSX, Remotion-style npx kinetograph init --html # or an HTML / HyperFrames page npm install ``` `init` makes `src/` for code (or `html/` for a page), `public/` for images, fonts, audio and video, and `out/` for everything Kinetograph writes. It also writes a starter title card. Render it: ```sh npx kinetograph render src/index.tsx # writes out/renders/Main.mp4 npx kinetograph render html/index.html # for an HTML project ``` ## How it works Node runs your project and a Rust addon draws each frame on the GPU. The [Engine](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/internals/engine/) page walks through the six steps. ## Docs Everything else is on the docs site, [kinetograph.dev/docs](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/): - [Installation](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/getting-started/installation/) and [First video](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/getting-started/first-video/) - [Authoring](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/guides/authoring/) and [Remotion compatibility](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/compat/) - [Studio](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/guides/studio/), the local editor - [Use with agents](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/guides/agents/) - [Engine](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/internals/engine/) and [What works](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/compat/) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [Contributing](https://kinetograph.dev/docs/contributing/)
Credits for the film's footage - "Blacksmith Scene" (Edison, 1893) and "Fred Ott's Sneeze" (Edison, 1894), public domain. - "Armistice Day Parade, Columbus, Ohio, 1927", US National Archives ([archive.org/details/111-h-1555](https://archive.org/details/111-h-1555)), a US government work. - SMPTE Universal Leader, public domain. - The handwritten "FILM" and the 16mm film burn are from licensed overlay packs ("Text Animation Overlays" and "Custom Transitions: Film Burns"); they are not in the repo.
## License Kinetograph is open source under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE.md), free for any use, including commercial. Vendored crates keep their own licences ([vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)).

name: kinetograph
description: Entry point for making videos and motion graphics with Kinetograph, a video engine with no browser in it. Use first when asked to build, edit, preview or render a video, animation, title card or sound design with Kinetograph, or to run any `kinetograph` command; it says which kinetograph-* skill to load next.
metadata:
  version: "0.4.0-rc.1"
---

# Kinetograph

Kinetograph renders video without a browser. You write TypeScript with the Remotion API and a few native elements (or an
HTML page with GSAP, and HyperFrames projects render as they are); Node runs it; a GPU compositor draws it. You cannot
watch a video, so you look at single frames and read the scene graph.

Run everything as `npx kinetograph <command>`. Add `--json` to get one JSON object you can parse; a failure is
`{ "error": { "code", "message" } }` with exit code 1. Over MCP (`kinetograph mcp`) there is one tool per command except
`studio`, named like the command (`audio analyze` is `audio_analyze`), with the same arguments; `still`, `strip` and `onion`
return the image itself.

## Which skill

Load the one that fits the step, and read its SKILL.md before you act. They are installed together.

| When | Skill |
|---|---|
| Start a project or a composition, add a component, template or taste | `kinetograph-create` |
| Write or change a composition: layout, text, media, effects, sound, fonts, timing, plugins, what the engine draws | `kinetograph-markup` |
| Look at frames, check, export (`still`, `strip`, `onion`, `inspect`, `lint`, `render`, `doctor`) | `kinetograph-render` |
| The person wants to preview, mark up, tune props or answer a panel in Studio | `kinetograph-studio` |
| Look something up in the Kinetograph docs | `kinetograph-docs` |
| Update `kinetograph`, its packages and these skills | `kinetograph-upgrade` |
| Move an existing Remotion project onto Kinetograph | `kinetograph-migrate` |

## The loop

1. **Create** the project once (`kinetograph-create`).
2. **Write** the composition (`kinetograph-markup`).
3. **Look and check**: `strip` first, then `lint` and `inspect` (`kinetograph-render`). Fix and repeat; a still takes well
   under a second.
4. **Render** to a file (`kinetograph-render`).

Rendering is a pure function of the frame number: nothing reads the clock, and `random(seed)` is Remotion's.

## Out-of-date notices

If a Kinetograph command prints that the CLI or the skills are out of date (a line on stderr, a `notices` field in
`--json`, or an extra text part on the first MCP tool result), tell the user and ask whether to update. Don't update
without a yes; then use `kinetograph-upgrade`.
